subjects.introduction: What does it mean to be detached from all save God while working, loving and serving in the world? These 300 chosen quotations include every verified authorized selection in the compilation. They begin with definitions and qualifications: detachment concerns the attachment of the heart rather than the absence of means, and work in a profession is itself praised. The readings then move through the transience of the world, the surrender of self and will, the conditions of a seeker’s understanding, and the influence of detachment in service. Accounts of particular lives, many of them reported recollections, show renunciation in poverty, imprisonment and loss. A sequence on patience presents it as the highest fruit of detachment, and prayers for detachment close the linked readings. Gleanings section CXXVIII defines the world as unawareness of one’s Maker [1], and the Ishráqát ends with a counsel to be patient [2]. A letter written on behalf of Shoghi Effendi extends patience to oneself [3]. Short sayings from the Qur’án [4] and the Dhammapada [5] offer comparisons on patience and self-conquest without erasing the differences between traditions. The actual neighboring subjects connect this study with contentment, tranquillity, moderation, sacrifice, tests, trust in God and the transience of the physical world.
subjects.arc: What detachment is and is not → The transience of the world and the call to leave it behind → Self, will and motive → Detachment as a condition of understanding → Influence in service and teaching → Lives of renunciation and inward freedom → Patience as the fruit of detachment → Prayers for detachment

These readings call the reader to leave behind what the people possess. Their images of transience are vivid: a handful of clay that a child shapes, a cloud passing over, a web more frail than a spider’s, the waves of the sea, a world that is not a homeland. Several are addressed to particular people, including the Pope and the high priests, and their setting matters. Read the language of renunciation together with the qualifications that precede it rather than as contempt for life or for other people; one of those passages says that the world loved in relation to God is accepted. What, exactly, do these readings ask a person to leave? How might an image of transience change a choice made today?

Which passage best shows how surrender of will can coexist with responsibility?

How does detachment affect what a person is able to see and to say?
